memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So Moses wrote down this law and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and to all the elders of Israel. Then Moses commanded them: 'At the end of every seven years, in the year for canceling debts, during the Festival of Tabernacles, when all Israel comes to appear before the Lord your God at the place he will choose, you shall read this law before them in their hearing.'" — Deut 31:9-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses did something vital before he died: he wrote the law down. Rather than leaving God's words to fade in fickle human memory, he preserved them in writing and entrusted them to the priests and elders. And he commanded that they be read publicly every seven years, so that the whole nation — for generations to come — would keep hearing God's Word. He was making sure the truth would not be lost when he was gone.

This tells us how precious God's Word is, and how carefully it was preserved. The Scriptures we hold today did not come to us casually. God ensured His Word was written down, protected, and passed on faithfully across the centuries so that it could reach us. What a gift it is to possess the Word of God.

There is also a lesson here about the importance of hearing Scripture together. The law was to be read aloud to "all Israel" — men, women, children, all gathered to listen. God's people are nourished not only by private reading but by hearing His Word proclaimed in the gathered community.

Every word Moses preserved ultimately points to Christ, the living Word, "for these are the very Scriptures that testify about me," Jesus said (John 5:39). The Word was preserved so that we might come to know Him. So treasure your Bible. Read it, hear it, gather around it with God's people. It is the preserved, precious Word that leads us to the Saviour.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I treasure the Scriptures as the precious, preserved Word of God?
2. Am I nourished both by private reading and by hearing the Word with others?
3. How can I give God's Word a more central place in my life?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for preserving Your Word across the generations so it could reach me. Help me treasure it, read it, and gather around it with Your people, and let it lead me ever closer to Christ. Amen.
